latin: Inquantum opifex in forma unius uidet unum unius essentialis, facit deos mundanos illius partis; inquantum ens unius essentialis, facit angelos in eadem parte; in quantum uidet unum entis unialis, facit demones ibi; inquantum esse entis unialis, animalia ibidem facit.
latin_note: Line-end hyphenation in the OCR (farmer1998:16595-16598) is not reproduced in the Latin field.
translation: To the extent that the maker sees, in the form of the one, the one of the essentially one, he makes the worldly gods of that part; to the extent that he sees the being of the essentially one, he makes angels in the same part; to the extent that he sees the one of the one-like being, he makes demons there; to the extent that he sees the existing of the one-like being, he makes animals in that same place.
translation_note: 'unius essentialis' and 'entis unialis' are coined technical genitives; 'esse' is rendered 'existing' to keep it apart from 'ens' (being). The 'inquan-tum' break in the Latin is silent OCR line-hyphenation (farmer1998:16601).
